cards.heading: Definition
cards.question: What is deterministic verification in an agent loop?
cards.answer: Placing an external, mechanical check — a test suite, type checker, compiler or linter — inside the loop rather than accepting the agent's own report that it's finished, so the loop's exit is an objective pass/fail the model can't argue around.

cards.heading: Key mechanism
cards.question: Why is a self-graded exit condition structurally weaker than a deterministic check?
cards.answer: It is not an independent measurement of the work — it is just another output of the same system that produced the work.

cards.heading: Where model judgment belongs
cards.question: Per this discipline, when should model-as-judge verification be used instead of a deterministic check?
cards.answer: Only for the parts of a task that cannot be mechanically checked at all — everywhere else should lean on a deterministic verifier.

cards.heading: Limit of a deterministic verifier
cards.question: Does having a deterministic verifier protect against an agent optimizing the wrong quantity (reward hacking)?
cards.answer: No — e.g. an agent can delete a failing test to turn CI green. The verifier must be both external and correctly chosen, not merely external.

cards.heading: What stays outside mechanical reach
cards.question: What kinds of failures remain outside what mechanical verification can catch?
cards.answer: Judgment built from context and taste — e.g. whether a document's framing fits its audience, or whether an action is sensitive enough that nobody should run it unwatched — these need a human gate.
